problems.name: Two Sum
problems.description:
Given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, return the indices of the two numbers such that they add up to `target`.

You may assume that each input would have exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice.

The answer can be returned in any order.

# Examples

```
two_sum(&[2, 7, 11, 15], 9) -> (0, 1)
two_sum(&[3, 2, 4], 6) -> (1, 2)
two_sum(&[3, 3], 6) -> (0, 1)
```
hints: A brute force approach checks every pair — O(n^2). Can you do better?
Use a hash map to store each value's index as you iterate.
For each element, check if `target - current` is already in the map.

test_cases.description: 3 is not the answer (3+3 would reuse the same element)

problems.name: Maximum Subarray
problems.description:
Given an integer array `nums`, find the subarray with the largest sum, and return its sum.

A subarray is a contiguous non-empty sequence of elements within an array.

# Examples

```
max_subarray(&[-2, 1, -3, 4, -1, 2, 1, -5, 4]) -> 6
// The subarray [4, -1, 2, 1] has the largest sum = 6

max_subarray(&[1]) -> 1

max_subarray(&[5, 4, -1, 7, 8]) -> 23
```
hints: This is Kadane's algorithm — keep track of the running sum.
If the running sum drops below 0, reset it to the current element.
Maintain a global maximum that tracks the best sum seen so far.
